chronology: Recap: Aghora (Steelhead's daughter; female body with twin brother's brain) hides on garden planet Flos to give birth after destroying a universe-scale enemy and mercy-killing Deyanira the tarantuwolf.

The four surviving whore-priestesses of Shabda-Oud travel covertly toward Kgen-Kgen prison in an octocyborg, activating an invisibility shield and emptying their spirits against anticipated mental probes.
The priestesses breach Kgen-Kgen, bypass orbital defenses via a directed beam, and kill guards with combined psychic force.
The priestesses free Zombra from her planetary-scale cell; Zombra learns her rescuers are clan survivors nearly annihilated by the Metabaron and that their goal is galactic domination.

In a separate council chamber, conspirators cite a prophecy of a perfect androgyne ruler and plot to assassinate the Empress; a dark-haired woman warns that the Metabaron guards the Empress and has already defeated her.
Conspirators recruit a dark-haired female warrior to kill the nine-months-pregnant Aghora, exploiting her limited combat mobility; payment is a cloned kantylopter.
Zombra undergoes biomechanical reintegration, declares herself restored, and demonstrates her power to divide into millions of identical warrior-units that can later recombine.
The whore-priestesses unleash the Zombra swarm in the Gardens of Flos; Aghora, in labor, climbs Rock Dragonis while the Metabaron fights as rearguard against overwhelming numbers.
Surrounded at the summit of Rock Dragonis, Aghora mentally redirects the metablade's battle-hunger against itself, sacrificing the weapon and using its explosion to escape.
Aghora and the newborn escape through Flos's pollen layer aboard the Metacraft; she orders a flaming maxi-oko deployed and feeds the infant artificial milk.
The armored leader with the brain-entity Crow destroys planet Flos, incinerating the Zombras and all flora, then sets course for the Golden Planet to engineer treachery against the Empire.
Crow approaches the Golden Planet, finds the Endoguard drifting, and presses on; inside the assembly chamber, witches overwhelm delegates with mental force.
A bald man defends the Empress against the witches invoking Bushitaka's 'Victory or Death'; the infant crawls unharmed through crossing mental beams toward Aghora.
The baby's diamond-bright eyes appear to destroy the attacking force; fighting ends.
The imperial court awards the infant the title Trino-Viscount, a high-nobility medallion, and three billion kiblars.
Aghora refuses to give the child a personal name, designating him No-Name and declaring him destined to be the perfect warrior and technopope.
Frame narrative: Tonto recounts these events to Master Lothar; Lothar dismembers Tonto piece by piece for interruptions until Tonto submits and agrees to narrate properly.
locations: Kgen-Kgen — the Empire's titanium prison satellite
Planet Flos — a garden planet surrounded by a pollen layer; destroyed by end of volume
Rock Dragonis — mystical rock formation at Flos, said to have grown from the buried head of the last dragon
Gardens of Flos — site of the Zombra ambush
The Golden Planet — seat of the Empress; site of the climactic battle with the witches
Imperial court ceremonial chamber — where the infant is formally honored
Aboard the Metacraft — escape route from Flos and approach vector to the Golden Planet
lore_laws: Bushitaka doctrine: a warrior's survival may require self-sacrifice; its motto is 'Victory or Death.'
A Metabaron can be withheld from imperial military action under disputed circumstances and is formally recognized by the Imperial Court.
Emptying one's spirits is a known defense against mental probing.
Robotic law governs how one machine may address another; identity circuits are removable and can be stripped as punishment.
An entire planet can be constructed to contain a sufficiently dangerous prisoner.
The metablade possesses a battle-hunger that its wielder can mentally redirect; turned against itself, it self-destructs.
Kgen-Kgen is the Empire's most dreaded prison, a titanium satellite.
The imperial court can bestow noble decorations, hereditary titles, and monetary rewards; the currency unit is kiblars.
Spirit transfer into a genetically modified body exists as a technology.
A kantylopter is a major source of individual power and capability; a destroyed specimen can be cloned from a recovered cell.
major_events: The four surviving whore-priestesses of Shabda-Oud break Zombra out of Kgen-Kgen, a prison whose containment required an entire dedicated planet.
Zombra is biomechanically restored and demonstrates the ability to split into millions of warrior-units that can recombine into one body.
Conspirators recruit a female warrior to assassinate the nine-months-pregnant Aghora, offering a cloned kantylopter as payment.
The Zombra swarm ambushes Aghora in the Gardens of Flos during her labor, forcing the Metabaron into a last-stand rearguard action.
Aghora sacrifices the metablade by turning its battle-hunger against itself, using the resulting explosion to escape.
Aghora gives birth on Rock Dragonis and escapes Flos aboard the Metacraft.
Planet Flos is completely destroyed; all Zombras and the planet's flora are incinerated.
The baby's diamond-bright eyes neutralize the psychic attackers threatening the Empress at the Golden Planet.
The imperial court honors the infant as Trino-Viscount with a medallion and three billion kiblars.
Aghora declares the child will carry no personal name — No-Name — and is destined to be both the perfect warrior and the supreme technopope.
open_uncertainties: The exact identity and name of the dark-haired female warrior recruited to assassinate Aghora are not established.
The identities of the cybernetic council conspirators are not given.
The precise nature of what was restored inside Zombra during biomechanical reintegration is not shown explicitly.
Whether the baby's diamond-bright eyes directly caused the destruction of the attacking force is implied but not stated.
The identity of the armored leader traveling with Crow is not confirmed.
The exact nature of Crow — living brain, ship intelligence, or otherwise — is ambiguous.
The two-headed ape-like claimant at the council who presents itself as the prophetic androgyne has no confirmed name.
Whether the battle imagery shown alongside the Tonto-Lothar frame represents live events, recounted memory, or a visualization is not made explicit.
Printed page numbers visible in the art differ from the supplied page labels on at least two pages; no explanation is given.
The identity of the bald man who defends the Empress invoking Bushitaka is not confirmed.
recurring_motifs: Androgyny and dual identity: Aghora's female body housing a male twin's brain; the prophecy of a perfect androgyne ruler; the newborn referred to as his father-mother's child.
Creation of life amid mass destruction: Aghora's labor and delivery simultaneous with the Zombra assault and the annihilation of Flos.
Self-sacrifice as the path to survival: Aghora destroys the metablade to escape; Bushitaka's maxim frames sacrifice as warrior law.
Mental and psychic force as the dominant weapon: priestesses use combined psycho-essence; Zombra has swarm-division; witches project energy beams; the baby is immune to mental attack.
The Metabaron as an insurmountable obstacle: conspirators, the recruited warrior, and the whore-priestesses all define their plans around defeating or bypassing him.
The robotic narrator frame: Tonto recounts events to Master Lothar under coercion, providing an ironic and interrupted perspective on the heroic story.
Destruction of worlds: Aghora previously destroyed a universe; Flos is annihilated here; mini-bombs are threatened against the Golden Planet.
title: The Return of The Shabda-Oud
